conversations.content: Declined to log in to the competition platform with the password or submit on the contestant's behalf; asked for the task statement. Found that upstream 2026-competition-round2 was an empty template (empty Dockerfile and conversation.json) and that the fork already had an earlier Go MiniVectorDB (M1-M4) whose README marked protocol, error codes and ANN requirements as 待确认.
Pushing to sleepz1/seekdb was refused (Claude GitHub App not installed for the repo); offered patch delivery instead.

Provided the task statement (U4) and, after the Yuque page could not be opened from the agent's browser, copied the full page text manually (U6-U8), which contained the link to the official public cases.

Fetched upstream round2 commit a3dba559 'upload some cases': mysqltest/README.md, manifest.json and 5 cases. Read off the semantics: vectors are quoted strings '[0, 2]'; L2_DISTANCE is not squared; alias usable in ORDER BY; ties by primary key; .result uses columns/rows/affected_rows/unordered; floats compared with 1e-5. The README states the driver framing is not included, so stdout framing remains unknown.

Decision: rewrite instead of extending the old engine, because it cloned the whole in-memory database per transaction and could not meet 'data larger than the memory limit'. New design: one CRC32C-framed append-only commit log in /data with fdatasync before acknowledging; in-memory PK index + slots with a memory-budgeted row cache (pread for the rest); per-transaction change map; torn-tail truncation on recovery; atomic compaction via temp file + rename.

Output format chosen as one JSON line per statement mirroring the .result field names, with --format tsv as a fallback, because the official driver framing is unpublished. To be checked with the platform's free environment pre-check.

Performance hypothesis H1: the 3.4 ms/query cost is the generic ORDER BY path allocating a key slice per row. Added an allocation-free L2 TopK heap. Result: 3.43 -> 3.14 ms/query; hypothesis mostly wrong. Profiling then showed Go map iteration (random memory order) dominating; scanning the slot array linearly gave 2.97 -> 1.21 ms/op.

Hypothesis H2: early termination of the distance loop against the current K-th distance will cut work. Result: 1.21 -> 1.27 ms/op, no gain: on uniform random 128-d data distances concentrate, so partial sums rarely exceed the bound. Kept it because it is exact (margin 1e-9 on the squared bound so pk tie-breaks cannot change) and may help on clustered data.

Hypothesis H3: the container has a CPU quota (task example --cpus=2) that Go 1.22 ignores; split large scans across min(NumCPU, cgroup quota) workers and merge by (distance, pk). Result end to end: 3.14 -> 0.84 ms/query. Added a test proving parallel == sequential on data with many exact ties.
Framing issue found while testing: a statement split over lines without ';' was cut at the newline. Changed to adaptive framing: newline ends a statement only until the first ';' is observed.

record.record_type: Continuation summary, not a verbatim conversation transcript
record.language_rationale: Keep the working Go engine; the standard library supplies TCP, JSON and filesystem support, and a CGO-disabled build produces a standalone binary for a small scratch Docker image.

protocol.now: Confirmed judging path: foreground stdin SQL, stdout TSV/results/status, stderr logs. Default /data; no listener.
protocol.framing: Temporary until round2 pack: semicolons outside SQL single quotes; newline outside quotes and parentheses/brackets; doubled quotes supported; EOF executes pending SQL and exits. Pending official pack / 待确认.
protocol.results: SELECT: TSV column header, rows, OK <rowcount>. Text escapes backslash/tab/newline/carriage return; vectors JSON arrays. Other success: OK <affected>. SQL failure: ERROR <message>, then continue. Responses flushed immediately.
protocol.wire_optional: Explicit -mysql-addr or -addr replaces stdin with retained MySQL helper; empty default. Permissive auth remains. Primary smoke never uses TCP.
protocol.correction: Supersedes M3 assumption that MySQL wire was the primary judging path.
protocol.ready: No ready flag/unsolicited line. Local SELECT 1 readiness probe. Official flag/handshake pending official pack / 待确认.
protocol.error_codes: ERROR <message>, continue; no numeric SQL codes. Official codes pending official pack / 待确认.

persistence.method: One newline-delimited JSON committed transaction record containing sequential LSN and successful deterministic write statements; append and fsync before publish/acknowledge. Autocommit uses one statement. WAL creation and recovery truncation are synced; directory is synced on Open.
persistence.recovery: Load optional legacy snapshot, replay contiguous complete WAL records. Truncate incomplete tail before accepting writes. Reject malformed complete records and sequence gaps. No new full snapshots; no checkpoint/compaction yet. Snapshot JSON uses UseNumber and schema normalization to int64/string/[]float32; transaction copies preserve types.
persistence.failure: Write/sync error blocks further durable writes until restart. Interrupted/unacknowledged commit can have uncertain outcome. One Engine/server per directory; no process lock.

ANN is deterministic every-second filtered-candidate sampling, not an index; no recall guarantee, may return fewer than k rows; performance/quality work remains.
First BIGINT is temporary PK tie key; uniqueness not enforced. Float32 distance arithmetic can overflow and return ERROR.

questions_and_decisions: Confirmed official foreground stdin/stdout judging correction; wire optional only.
Keep M3 fsynced committed transaction records and immutable snapshot base.
Use documented temporary TSV framing pending official pack.
Local validation, commit and branch push authorized; no official submission, PR merge, secrets or build artifacts in git.
M4 uses int64 for INT/INTEGER/BIGINT; VARCHAR(n) counts Unicode runes; vectors store and accumulate float32.
Temporary PK: first BIGINT, ascending on equal score even with DESC; no uniqueness enforcement.
Exact default; ANN samples filtered insertion-order offsets 0,2,4,... before distance sorting; distinct code path and output tested.
SET search_mode is session configuration, not transactional or durable; SELECT search_mode is diagnostic.

transactions.semantics: BEGIN or START TRANSACTION clones committed state; read-your-writes; no dirty reads. COMMIT checks database-wide version and logs successful statements atomically. ROLLBACK/disconnect discard private state. No in-flight transaction enters WAL. Failed statements leave preceding successful statements intact. Conflicts require ROLLBACK.
transactions.client: One stdin process uses one Session; EOF discards private transaction. Optional wire still supports pinned connection via repeated -query flags.
